The rule expands qualifying service for the 12-month FMLA eligibility requirement to include nearly all federal civilian service, including temporary and intermittent employment, as well as service with USPS, the Postal Regulatory Commission, and certain nonappropriated fund entities. It also allows honorable active service in the Army, Navy, Air Force, Space Force, or Marine Corps to count toward eligibility, but excludes Coast Guard and Public Health Service commissioned-corps service. The revisions clarify that annual and sick leave earned under non-title 5 authorities may be substituted for unpaid FMLA leave and exclude certain Veterans Health Administration employees covered by a separate VA leave system from title 5 FMLA coverage. The rule would take effect December 14, 2026, unless OPM receives significant adverse comments by November 16, 2026, and the changes also affect eligibility for paid parental leave.
